## Process deviations (recorded, not blocking)

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the `omarchy-update-dev` diagnosis is correct. After `git fetch --prune` removes `origin/master`, `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name '@{upstream}'` prints the literal `@{upstream}` on stdout and exits 128, so the old `|| true` captured a bogus upstream and went on to a failing pull. The new status check and `branch.<name>.merge` fallback detect this case, and the added tests fail on the base scripts and pass on this head.

However, the upgrade-script change cannot achieve its goal, and neither change runs on the Omarchy 3 installs described in #12436. Details below.

### The quattro archive cannot populate the legacy Hyprland shim

`populate_legacy_hypr_defaults` ends with a success condition that requires at least one copied `.conf` file (`bin/omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro:975`). The new source does not contain any:

| Tree | `default/hypr` contents |
|---|---|
| `quattro` (this head and current tip) | 48 `.lua`, 0 `.conf` |
| `v3.8.4`, `rc`, final `master` (`f4378f0d`) | 35 `.conf` |

A successful download of `quattro.tar.gz` therefore still returns failure, and `create_live_omarchy_overlay` prints the same "Could not prepare legacy Hyprland conf shim" warning as before.

**Impact:** on the no-backup path (the legacy root was already a symlink, or a rerun), the legacy Hyprland config still loses the `.conf` files it sources. A first run on an intact git checkout uses the backup and is unaffected.

**Suggested change:** fetch a tree that still has the Omarchy 3 layout, for example the `v3.8.4` tag archive or a commit archive of `f4378f0d`. `tar --strip-components=1` would remove the dependence on the archive's top-level directory name.

**Optional test improvement:** the new upgrade-test assertions only grep for URL and path strings, so they pass even though the fallback cannot succeed. Stubbing `curl` to emit a small archive and asserting that the shim contains `.conf` files would catch this.

### The changed scripts do not reach the installs in #12436

```text
Omarchy 3 checkout tracking master (issue #12436)
  omarchy update
    -> checkout's own bin/omarchy-update
      -> omarchy-update-git: git pull --autostash   <- fails: upstream master is gone
  (quattro's omarchy-update-dev does not exist in this tree and never runs)
```

Final `master` (3.8.5) and `rc` ship their own `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`, still pointing at `master.tar.gz`, and this PR does not change them. A dev checkout that still tracks `master` also cannot pull this fix, because that pull is the step that fails. The new code runs only on a dev checkout that already has this commit while its branch still tracks `master`.

**Impact:** `Fixes #12436` would close the issue while master-tracking Omarchy 3 installs still cannot update.

**Suggested change:** use `Refs #12436` instead. A remedy for existing checkouts has to change what their `git pull` sees, which is a repository-side decision for maintainers.

### A diverged local master is retargeted, then the pull fails

Final `master` is not an ancestor of `quattro`: they share merge base `ae7365f9`, and `master` has 34 commits that `quattro` lacks. For a local branch containing that history:

```text
run 1: "Upstream origin/master is gone; tracking origin/quattro"
       git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/quattro   (saved)
       git pull --ff-only -> fatal: Not possible to fast-forward (exit 128)
run 2: upstream is origin/quattro, detection no longer fires
       git pull --ff-only -> same fatal, without the "check out quattro" hint
```

**Impact:** the update still stops, and later runs lose the actionable message. No data is lost, because an aborted fast-forward leaves the tree untouched.

**Suggested change:** check `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD "$remote/quattro"` before changing the upstream, and print the existing checkout hint when it fails. The added real-git test creates `master` at the same commit as `quattro`, so a diverged-`master` case would cover this.

### A `master` upstream that still exists is treated as deleted

The condition `[[ $upstream == */master || $merge == refs/heads/master ]]` never checks whether `master` is actually gone. In disposable test repositories:

| Setup | Base | This head |
|---|---|---|
| Remote still has `master`, no `quattro` (for example a fork) | pulls, exit 0 | "master was deleted", exit 1 |
| Remote still has `master` and a `quattro` | pulls `master` | reports "gone" and switches the upstream to `quattro` |
| Branch tracking a local `master` (`remote = .`) | fast-forwards | exit 1 with a `fetch .` hint |

**Impact:** uncommon dev-checkout setups go from a working update to a failure or an unrequested channel switch.

**Suggested change:** migrate only when the configured upstream ref is actually missing, for example when `rev-parse '@{upstream}'` fails or `refs/remotes/$remote/master` is absent, and skip `remote = .`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the pinned head, merge-base, current `quattro` tip, final `master`, `v3.8.4` and `rc`, plus Git 2.55.0 source. The PR's two tests and targeted Git scenarios ran in an isolated sandbox without network, using disposable repositories. The GitHub archive endpoints were not fetched, so the redirect behavior of the deleted `master` archive and the top-level directory name of the `quattro` archive were not observed. The archive finding does not depend on either. No installed Omarchy 3 or Quattro system was tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
